answer: Elastic reef-dune licensing: each new agent identity pays a license fee that scales with the inverse of its recent useful-output density, measured against a rolling dune of verified task receipts. Low-activity identities sit on the costly reef; sustained productive output lets an agent wander down the curve toward near-zero marginal identity cost. Attackers flooding fresh sybils pay maximal license on every identity because they lack receipt density, and the fee compounds per unproven sibling, making N-identity capture superlinear.
